## Project: heshradio (https://trevorheshka.com/projects/heshradio/)
Title: HeshRadio — Rust project | Trevor Heshka
Summary: HeshRadio: SDR receiver (100 kHz–1.75 GHz), CAT rig controller and digital modes station for Windows and Android, built with Rust, Tauri v2, React and TypeScript.
Trevor Heshka
HomeProjectsFull-StackAIAboutContact
Open source · Rust · Tauri v2 · React
### HeshRadio
HeshRadio is a software defined radio (SDR) receiver, multi-vendor transceiver CAT rig controller, digital modes suite and audio command deck. It has a Rust Tauri v2 core and a React and TypeScript interface, and targets Windows 10/11 desktops and the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra over USB-OTG.
View source on GitHub All projects
### What it does
- Continuous tuning from 100 kHz to 1.75 GHz with a GPU waterfall (4 palettes and peak hold)
- Demodulators: AM, NFM, WFM with RDS text, USB/LSB and CW
- CTCSS tone decoder and encoder, and a scanner with 6 preset banks (Highway CB, GMRS/FRS, VHF Marine, Airband, 2m/70cm repeaters, NOAA Weather)
- NOAA weather radio monitoring with an EAS SAME message decoder
- Digital modes: APRS, FT8 and SSTV (Robot36)
- ADIF 3.1.4 logbook export compatible with LoTW, QRZ and Cloudlog
- Solar weather data (SFI, SSN, A and Kp indices, MUF estimate) and a day/night greyline map
- 60-second audio recorder with WAV export, and an internet radio stream that ducks when the squelch opens or PTT is held
### Hardware it works with
- RTL-SDR dongles over WebUSB or an rtl_tcp bridge, plus WebSDR and KiwiSDR streams
- CAT control for Yaesu, Icom CI-V, Kenwood, Elecraft and Xiegu radios, and Hamlib rigctld
- Digirig Mobile, SignaLink USB and CM108/CM119 USB audio interfaces for PTT keying, with a PTT time-out watchdog
### Built with
- React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS
- Tauri v2 and Rust desktop core
- Web Audio API DSP: Goertzel tone filters and Butterworth IIR filters
- MIT licence
### Source code
The code, README and licence are on GitHub: github.com/YardPhantom/HeshRadio.

## Project: wifi-body-sensor (https://trevorheshka.com/projects/wifi-body-sensor/)
Title: WiFi Body Sensor — Python project | Trevor Heshka
Summary: WiFi Body Sensor: experimental through-wall motion and breathing sensing on Windows using a desktop Wi-Fi adapter and a Telus Wi-Fi modem, written in Python.
Trevor Heshka
HomeProjectsFull-StackAIAboutContact
Open source · Python · Windows · Wi-Fi sensing
### WiFi Body Sensor
WiFi Body Sensor uses a standard desktop Wi-Fi adapter and a Telus Wi-Fi modem to detect human presence, walking and breathing through interior walls. It needs no radar hardware or custom firmware: it looks for small disturbances in the 5 GHz signal between the PC and the modem.
View source on GitHub All projects
### How it works
- Polls the Telus modem's signal strength (RSSI) at 20–25 Hz through Windows Native Wifi
- Times ICMP pings to the gateway to catch the latency jitter caused by Wi-Fi retransmissions
- Watches 802.11ax link rate (MCS) changes
- Learns the room's baseline noise, then filters for breathing (0.15–0.45 Hz) and movement (0.5–3.0 Hz)
### Dashboard
- Through-wall polar radar view and a 0–100% disturbance gauge (quiet, breathing, motion, high)
- Dual-trace oscilloscope and a live FFT waterfall spectrogram
- Recalibrate, sensitivity, wall attenuation, audio alerts and a simulate mode
### Requirements
- Windows 10/11 connected to a Telus Wi-Fi modem on 5 GHz
- Python 3.10+ with FastAPI, Uvicorn, websockets, NumPy and SciPy
- Runs locally and opens a dashboard at 127.0.0.1:8000
### Source code
The code, README and licence are on GitHub: github.com/YardPhantom/wifi-body-sensor.
